question: A grocery seller mixes two varieties of tea costing Rs. 300 per kg and Rs. 160 per kg in such a ratio that by selling this mixture at the rate of Rs. 187 per kg the shopkeeper earns 10% profit. In what respective ratio does the grocery seller mix the two varieties of tea?
solution:
**Given:**

A grocery seller mixes two varieties of tea costing Rs. 300 per kg and Rs. 160 per kg in such a ratio that by selling this mixture at the rate of Rs. 187 per kg the shopkeeper earns 10% profit.

**Formula Used:**

Let the cost price of the mixture be C.

Selling price = Cost price + Profit

Profit = 10% of Cost price

Using the weighted average formula for the two varieties of tea:

 C = ((300 times x + 160 times y))/(x + y) 

Given selling price = Rs. 187 per kg

Profit = 10%

So, Selling price = Cost price × 1.10

⇒ 187 = C × 1.10

⇒ C = 1871.10" id="MathJax-Element-79-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1871.10 1871.10 \frac{187}{1.10}

**Calculation:**

⇒ C = 170

Using the weighted average formula:

 170 = ((300 times x + 160 times y))/(x + y) 

⇒ 170(x + y) = 300x + 160y

⇒ 170x + 170y = 300x + 160y

⇒ 170y - 160y = 300x - 170x

⇒ 10y = 130x

⇒ y/x = 13/1

**∴ The correct answer is 1 ∶ 13.**
